note: Regrouped by CONCERN. The source is a single squash; the ten original commits named in its header are not recoverable from it, so these group boundaries are a reviewed regrouping, not a recovery. The split is lossless and machine-checked (see MANIFEST.md).

groups.title: Build & tooling
groups.why: The Android build entrypoint and the Go module pins. Nothing compiles without it, so it leads the series.

groups.title: Paths & runtime locations
groups.why: Android has no /var/lib and no writable /etc: daemon state must live under /data/adb. Establishes where the daemon reads and writes before anything else moves.

groups.title: TUN, netstack & netns
groups.why: The Android boundary: a pre-opened TUN fd handed in by the module, namespace handling, and the netstack that terminates traffic inside the daemon.

groups.title: DNS manager (Android)
groups.why: There is no resolv.conf on Android. The manager must set resolver properties directly and must not clobber netd's own view of the network.

groups.title: Routing & firewall
groups.why: Android's netd owns the policy tables. Route, mark and iptables handling must coexist with netd's rules rather than replace them - the highest-risk area in the series.

groups.title: Network monitor
groups.why: Wi-Fi and cellular handovers must be observed rather than polled blindly; Android's netlink surface differs from desktop Linux.

groups.title: Hostinfo & OS user
groups.why: Platform identity for the coordination server, plus the passwd and group lookups Android simply does not provide.

groups.title: CLI & feature knobs
groups.why: The user-facing switches: tailscale up / set behaviour on a platform with no desktop session, and the env knobs that gate Android-only features.

groups.title: Daemon integration
groups.why: How the local API, the peer API and the cert endpoints behave when the daemon runs as root outside an app sandbox.

groups.title: SSH & Taildrop
groups.why: The two features the stock Android app never exposed: Tailscale SSH and Taildrop, with Android-safe file operations.

groups.title: Self-update & version gate
groups.why: In-place OTA is impossible for a systemless module, so the self-updater is replaced and the version-format check is neutralised.

groups.title: Web surface
groups.why: tsweb adaptations for serving behind the module's local listener.
